pr_body:
If the command buffer is empty the shell was trying to read a string from a random memory location. Added a condition checking "argc" value when the select command is executed.

Fixes: #27227

Signed-off-by: Jakub Rzeszutko <jakub.rzeszutko@nordisemi.no>

issue_context.title: shell crashes on qemu_x86 board upon the Tab button press
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The program is interrupted when the user presses the `Tab` button in the shell.

**To Reproduce**
1. Modify shell_module sample by adding `CONFIG_SHELL_CMDS_SELECT=y` to the prj.conf file.
2. Run application for the qemu_x86 board:
`west build -b qemu_x86 -t run`
3. Once program is started hit the `TAB` button.
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
The shell is printing all available commands.

**Impact**
It is not possible to display all shell root commands. User experience is highly affected.

**Logs and console output**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34125330/88783287-deb22700-d18e-11ea-8978-6785d62b7797.png)


**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux Ubuntu 18.04
 - Toolchain: zephyr-sdk-0.11.3 
 - Commit SHA: 5e2e7a0fcf6f9815080e5fb311808730ccf3cbeb


**Additional context**
I can reproduce this error only on qemu_x86 board. It seems there is an error that the shell is trying to read a string from a random memory location. This error is not occurring when there at least 1 character in the command buffer.

review_comments: Because I cannot guarantee that `(*argc > 0)` will be checked before `strcmp("select", (*argv)[0]) == 0)`
Evaluation order is guaranteed to be left-to-right by standard
Ok, I've educated myself :) I will fix it
